stack.rule: Optional, not part of the default product runtime. Requires explicit performance and accessibility review.

stack.title: Material Symbols

stack.rule: Use as raw material, not as Material Design. Every icon gets a semantic role and accessible name policy.

referencePolicy.rule: The reference project is a benchmark, not a paste source. Reference parity is not the goal; product correctness is the goal.

decisions.rationale: Use the depth and page model, but adapt examples to fleet, driver, card, route, station, dashboard, authentication, and configuration work.
Literal copying imports assumptions and hides product gaps.
Components must use this system naming: button, select, card, etc.
The requested icon system is Material Symbols, governed by Symbol and Iconography.
The documentation depth is useful, but the contract must cover all foundations and this product risk, permission, telemetry, and accessibility rules.
Reference-style examples are useful only when they become explicit product examples, not generic cards.
Templates must prove different product contexts, not repeat a card layout with changed labels.

decisions.area: Canvas visual benchmark from external ZIP
decisions.rationale: Use the ZIP as a visual and product-behavior benchmark for richness, rhythm, microinteraction, states, and concrete mobility examples. Do not import its raw color, typography, spacing, radius, shadow, props, inline styles, or platform assumptions unless they are translated through Design System foundations, primitives, semantic tokens, contracts, and audit gates.

decisions.area: External ZIP tokens and component APIs
decisions.rationale: The ZIP may inform composition and quality targets, but Design System keeps its own foundations and primitives. Component scale remains owned by Density, typography by Voice, color by Energy, motion by Momentum, maps by Maps, charts by Charts, and accessibility by Accessibility.

Card may adapt the ZIP surface rhythm, hover lift, selected state, and product-specific content density only through Design System tokens, Edenred/Ubuntu typography, Density-owned scale, semantic state, Accessibility, and the no-nested-decorative-card rule. Reject inline styles, raw radii, raw shadows, public size props, and card-within-card composition.

blocking: No inherited prefixes such as eds-* or system-*.
No hex colors outside token declarations.
No raw px values outside token declarations.
Foundation and primitive inventory must match the machine-readable spec.
Foundation and primitive detail section functions must exist in the rendered app.
Gold components must expose component tokens.
maturityWarnings: Components need states, accessibility, responsive behavior, API, and tests.
Patterns need entry conditions, decision trees, failure modes, metrics, and components used.
Templates need realistic data, permissions, loading, empty, error, offline, recovery, and telemetry states.
qualityGates.definitionOfDone: An artifact is done only at maturity level 3 or 4.

operatingModel.renderedSurface: app.js documentation routes fed by packages/content/content/component-docs.json and packages/content/content/component-copy.json
operatingModel.rule: Machine-readable product rules, gates, inventories, artifact contracts, reference decisions, and maturity state live in specs or the auditor. Human-facing copy, examples, fixtures, and MIEL prompts live in packages/content/content/component-copy.json and must be audited against packages/specs/specs/unison.system.json before scaling.

agentContract.humanReadableSurface: app.js rendered documentation routes fed by packages/content/content/component-copy.json
agentContract.syncRule: Machine-readable contracts in packages/specs/specs/unison.system.json govern technical validity. Visible documentation and fixtures in packages/content/content/component-copy.json may explain and demonstrate those contracts, but cannot introduce states, props, variants, foundations, or rejection rules that contradict the spec. packages/audit/scripts/audit-system.js must verify the crossing before content is considered trustworthy.
rejectIf: The artifact exposes raw token values as public API.
The artifact skips foundations or primitive dependencies.
The artifact uses emoji or text placeholders instead of governed iconography.
The artifact requires animation to understand a task.
The artifact lacks accessibility behavior for name, role, state, focus, keyboard, contrast, reduced motion, or recovery.
The artifact creates a chart without an accessible text summary.
The artifact creates a map without permission-denied and fallback-list behavior.

validation: Artifact must declare layer and platform.
Components must include anatomy, states, accessibility, engineering, and agent spec.
Patterns must include journey, screens, metrics, research, engineering, and agent spec.
Templates must include context, IA, flows, data, permissions, implementation, and agent spec.
Charts must include accessible text summaries.
Maps must include permission-denied and fallback-list behavior.
Lottie cannot be required for task comprehension.
Material Symbols cannot replace accessible labels for rare or risky actions.
patterns: Mobile Card Detail and Quick Actions

motion.rule: Use for UI behavior that explains structure or state.

illustrativeAnimation.rule: Use for teaching or emotional clarity; never for required task comprehension.

editorialMotion.rule: Optional and gated by performance and accessibility review.

icons.rule: Use as raw icon material, not as Material Design. Every icon needs a semantic role and accessible-name policy.

charts.rule: Every chart needs title, description, text summary, color-safe encoding, empty state, and keyboard-reachable data access.

maps.rule: Map flows must include geolocation permission, denied state, fallback list, station detail, and route handoff.

invariants: Every artifact has human guidance and machine-readable specification.
Motion communicates cause, continuity, priority, feedback, or status.
Accessibility is a governing foundation for every layer.
Generic industry templates are excluded unless they serve the fleet product domain.
systemSpec.purpose: Make product decisions durable for designers, developers, product managers, content designers, researchers, service designers, and AI agents.
systemSpec.domain: Fleet, driver mobile, fleet manager desktop, cards, movements, routes, stations, dashboards, authentication, and configuration
systemSpec.name: Design System OS

energy.name: Energy
energy.purpose: Assign semantic meaning to color and visual intensity so users can identify action, status, risk, feedback, and surface hierarchy without guessing.

roles.use: Primary route, card, configuration, recovery actions, selected controls, focus-adjacent emphasis, navigation, and links.
Completed route handoff, successful card unblock, saved permissions.
Station availability risk, limit warning, stale dashboard data.
Warning text, icon, border, and progress color on light surfaces.
Blocked route, declined movement, permission failure, destructive confirmation.
Page, card, panel, sheet, table, and map surfaces.
Separators, controls, tables, selected and focused surfaces.

productExamples.example: Primary route action uses action energy; unavailable route uses error energy with recovery copy.
Block card uses error energy; quick actions and selected controls use action energy unless risk changes.
Warnings mark thresholds; success confirms resolved exceptions; surfaces stay calm for scanability.
Permission destructive actions use error energy and preserve audit context.

agentInstructions: Never choose color by appearance alone; map it to action, status, feedback, risk, or surface.

For filled interactive status, choose ramp and foreground together: warning uses yellow 400/500/600 with neutral 900; danger uses red 500/600/700 with text-on-action; success uses green 500/600/700 with text-on-action; action uses blue 500/600/700 with text-on-action. For warning text, icons, borders, and progress fills on light surfaces, use the warning foreground role instead of the filled yellow role.
Preserve status identity in loading and disabled states when risk intent matters.
Do not introduce new color families outside ref.energy.* without updating this contract.
rejectIf: Color is used decoratively without semantic role.
Filled status changes foreground color across default, hover, or pressed states without a documented contrast reason.
A chart or map relies only on color without accessible text/shape encoding.
A component defines hardcoded hex values outside Energy tokens.

voice.name: Voice
voice.purpose: Define typographic hierarchy and product language so content, numerals, and decisions are scannable, actionable, respectful, and consistent across mobile and desktop.

roles.use: Major page or template identity with Edenred Black.
Section titles and product hierarchy with Edenred Black.
KPIs, metrics, balances, counts, dashboard values, and prominent operational numbers with Edenred Black.
Controls, table headers, KPI labels, form labels with Ubuntu.
Body copy, guidance, explanations with Ubuntu.
Metadata, timestamps, helper text, secondary annotations.
Token names, API examples, agent-readable snippets.

productExamples.example: Display introduces the step; paragraph explains permission value; repair copy explains blocked recovery.
Labels remain terse; urgent copy explains risk without blaming the user.
KPI labels, deltas, legends, and summaries use distinct roles so fleet managers can scan quickly.
Permission warnings explain dependency and consequence before destructive action.

agentInstructions: Use Edenred Black only for display, heading, and numeral roles; use Ubuntu for all other product and UI text.
Write labels as objects or actions, not explanations.
Write repair copy with cause, next action, and ownership.
Keep agent and human spec language aligned.
rejectIf: Typography uses size or weight without semantic role.
Display text appears inside compact controls or dense tables.
Error copy states failure without recovery.
Agent specs omit content, localization, or accessibility consequences.

frame.name: Frame
frame.purpose: Govern spacing, grid, density, sizing, and responsive rhythm so product surfaces feel organized and never rely on one-off layout fixes.

roles.use: Inline gaps, component gaps, section rhythm, page rhythm.
Mobile, tablet, laptop, desktop content structure.
Compact operations, default product rhythm, comfortable review/touch flows.
Controls, cards, sheets, pills, panels.
Control heights, touch targets, dashboard modules, panels.
Controls, tables, selected surfaces, dividers.

productExamples.example: Card stack, quick actions, and movement rows use mobile margins and comfortable touch rhythm.
Map overlays and station detail panels use stable inset, sheet, and fallback list spacing.
12-column desktop grid aligns KPI tiles, charts, filter bar, and drill-down table.
Roles, permissions, drivers, and vehicles use dense table rhythm without losing focus target and hierarchy.

agentInstructions: Use Frame tokens for spacing, sizing, grid, border, and radius before changing CSS.
Declare density at the surface or page level; components should inherit it.
Avoid horizontal scroll in navigation and tab bars unless the component explicitly owns overflow behavior.
Check mobile, tablet, laptop, and desktop rhythm before calling a layout done.
rejectIf: Raw spacing, radius, border, or control size values are introduced outside tokens.
Content is wrapped in a container that reduces useful space without a hierarchy reason.
Navigation or tabs create unintended horizontal scrolling.
A component solves spacing locally instead of consuming Frame.

depth.name: Depth
depth.purpose: Define spatial hierarchy through surfaces, elevation, overlays, z-index, blur, and focus layering so users understand what is persistent, contextual, temporary, or blocking.

roles.use: Base app surface and dashboard canvas.
Cards, KPI tiles, station preview panels, table containers.
Menus, popovers, quick action clusters, map controls.
Sheets, modals, blocking review flows, permission gates.
Risk, destructive action, financial or role-change confirmations.
Transient confirmations and recovery messages.

productExamples.example: Bottom sheet sits above map controls but below blocking permission dialogs.
Drawer elevation separates contextual detail from persistent dashboard filters.
Role-change dialog blocks background actions and restores focus on close.
Topbar remains sticky without competing visually with active work surfaces.

agentInstructions: Choose depth by interaction priority, not by decoration.
Preserve focus order and escape behavior for every overlay.
Do not use arbitrary z-index values.
Use backdrop only when the background task must be paused.
rejectIf: Overlay lacks escape or focus restoration.
z-index is hardcoded outside Depth tokens.
A container is added only for decoration and reduces useful workspace.
Background content remains interactive behind blocking dialogs.

momentum.name: Momentum
momentum.purpose: Govern motion and transition so movement communicates cause, continuity, feedback, priority, and status without becoming required comprehension.

roles.use: Risk and accessibility fallback changes that must not delay comprehension.
Hover, press, focus, button feedback, small control transitions.
Tabs, filters, small panels, selected state updates.
Sheets, route transitions, onboarding moments.
Loading indicators with reduced-motion alternative.
Replace translation/scale with opacity, focus placement, and instant state.

productExamples.example: Spinner communicates work, but label and aria-busy carry the required information.
Map-to-station transition preserves spatial continuity; fallback list uses instant state update.
Sheet reveal explains change of context and restores focus after dismissal.
Chart refresh uses subtle state transition, not decorative movement.

agentInstructions: State the semantic reason for motion before choosing a preset.
Always define reduced-motion behavior.
Do not put required instructions only in animation.
Use dotLottie only for illustrative or teaching moments.
rejectIf: Motion is decorative only.
Reduced-motion behavior is missing.
Animation is required to understand the task.
Timing is hardcoded outside Momentum tokens.

state.name: State
state.purpose: Define interaction states, precedence, state composition, disabled behavior, loading behavior, validation, and assistive technology mapping.

roles.use: Available, stable, unselected baseline.
Pointer affordance without changing semantic value.
Keyboard and assistive navigation location.
Momentary activation feedback.
Chosen filter, tab, option, or row.
Pending operation; duplicate activation blocked.
Unavailable because permission, data, offline, risk, or future availability blocks action.
Recoverable or blocking failure with repair path.

productExamples.example: Open, focused, selected, loading, disabled, and error states remain distinct.

OTP loading blocks duplicate submit while preserving escape and retry.

agentInstructions: Resolve state precedence before styling.
Disabled must include reason when risk, permission, data, or offline blocks the user.
Focus must stay visible even when selected or error state is active.
Loading blocks duplicate activation.
rejectIf: Disabled is only opacity without reason.
Focus is suppressed by hover, selected, or error.
Loading can submit duplicate actions.
Error state lacks recovery or accessible announcement.

tone.name: Tone

rejectIf: Copy is decorative or vague.
Error copy lacks recovery.

roles.use: New concept, early pattern, or experiment.

dont: Do not nest decorative cards inside cards.

two-column comparison when content remains readable

Interactive Card is keyboard reachable and preserves focus visibility.
Default, hover, focus, selected, loading, error, disabled, and muted states remain distinct.
Mobile stack, desktop grid, and dense dashboard layouts do not overflow.
Surface, border, radius, padding, elevation, motion, icon, and text resolve through Design System tokens.
agentInstructions: Use Card for a single object, summary, or decision surface.
Move product sequencing and processs to patterns.
Preserve surface semantics, state, responsive behavior, and accessibility before adding visual richness.
rejectIf: Card is used as a decorative wrapper.

Product sequencing is hidden inside the base component.
State is color-only or recovery text is missing.
inventoryEscalations: CardStats maps to Card composition stats because the ZIP renders Card + mono value + Badge; KPI Tile owns dashboard thresholds, sparkline, and drill-in.
CardInteractive maps to Card interactive behavior, not a variant.
CardCompact maps to Card composition compact.
CardMedia maps to Card composition media.
CardElevated, CardMinimal, and CardGhost map to base Card variants.

input.purpose: Collect short free-form operational values while preserving label, value, helper, validation, loading, disabled, and keyboard behavior.
input.referenceRationale: Adopt the reference field discipline, but express surface, typography, state, density, and motion through Design System foundations and primitives.

anatomy.rule: Owns label, helper, validation, and state relationship.
Names the expected value and remains visible.
Holds typed value, placeholder, prefix, suffix, and focus ring.
Explains format, source, validation, or recovery.
Optional icon or qualifier supports the value without hiding state.
Optional reveal or clear behavior uses the internal Field Action primitive, inherits field density, keeps focus visible, and does not render an autonomous button container.

variants.use: Ordinary editable text capture.
Email capture with native keyboard and autocomplete.
Password capture with optional reveal affordance.
Numeric capture without formatting ownership.
Amount capture with prefix or suffix qualifiers.
Measurement capture with a unit suffix.
Short query capture that filters a current surface.

input.statePrecedence: disabled > loading > error > focus > filled > default

Energy.decision: Use Energy for input surface, border, filled emphasis, error identity, and disabled identity.
Energy.behavior: Energy changes field surface, state, and validation visibly.
Energy.example: Driver ID fields preserve neutral input rhythm and clear error identity.
Energy.test: Verify visual states, focus, and error contrast.
Energy.rejectIf: Energy is only named without changing field behavior.

Voice.decision: Use Voice for label, placeholder, value, helper, and recovery copy.
Voice.behavior: Voice keeps labels and recovery text readable at every density.
Voice.example: Search and wallet fields explain expected value before submission.
Voice.test: Verify label, helper, placeholder, and error text render.
Voice.rejectIf: The field relies on placeholder as the only label.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for field width, stacking, touch target, and grid fit.
Frame.behavior: Frame prevents overflow in mobile stacks and dense filters.
Frame.example: Fleet filters stack on small viewports and align in desktop grids.
Frame.test: Verify full-width, container, and viewport examples do not overflow.
Frame.rejectIf: The field uses fixed width outside its container.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only when the field action opens supporting UI.
Depth.behavior: Depth separates action affordance from the input surface.
Depth.example: Reveal, clear, or lookup affordances remain inside the field hierarchy.
Depth.test: Verify action affordance does not compete with validation.
Depth.rejectIf: Shadow is decorative or replaces state.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum for focus, loading, and reduced-motion feedback.
Momentum.behavior: Momentum communicates field response without delaying typing.
Momentum.example: Async validation shows progress without losing value.
Momentum.test: Verify reduced motion and loading behavior.
Momentum.rejectIf: Motion blocks input or hides validation.

State.decision: Use State to resolve disabled, loading, error, focus, filled, and default before styling.
State.behavior: State precedence controls styling and interaction.
State.example: Loading beats focus; disabled blocks interaction.
State.rejectIf: State is visual only or contradictory.

Tone.decision: Use Tone to keep field language direct and operational.
Tone.behavior: Tone removes ambiguous placeholder and error copy.
Tone.example: Use 'Enter driver ID' instead of vague instructions.
Tone.test: Verify recovery copy tells what to fix.
Tone.rejectIf: Copy blames the user or hides the fix.

Growth.decision: Use Growth for reusable field behavior across future input variants.
Growth.behavior: Growth keeps input API stable as masks or validation evolve.
Growth.example: Search, ID, amount, and code fields share the same foundation.
Growth.test: Verify props and state model remain portable.
Growth.rejectIf: A product field forks the component for one screen.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol for prefix, suffix, and action meaning.
Symbol.behavior: Symbols support the value without replacing label or helper.
Symbol.example: Search icon indicates lookup but label still names the input.
Symbol.test: Verify icon-only affordances have accessible names.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography for leading, trailing, loading, and error affordances.
Iconography.behavior: Icons inherit state and never introduce raw color.
Iconography.example: Error and progress icons follow field state.
Iconography.test: Verify icons inherit currentColor and accessible labels.
Iconography.rejectIf: Icons bypass tokens or duplicate label meaning.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility for visible labels, input semantics, describedby, error announcement, and focus.
Accessibility.behavior: Accessibility makes label, helper, error, disabled, and loading states machine-readable.
Accessibility.example: Validation links error text to the input.
Accessibility.test: Verify label, describedby, aria-invalid, keyboard, and screen reader output.
Accessibility.rejectIf: The field cannot be operated or understood without sight.

checkbox.name: Checkbox
checkbox.purpose: Use Checkbox for one independent boolean choice, item selection, or partial aggregate selection where the label must stay visible with checked, unchecked, indeterminate, focus, error, and disabled states.
checkbox.referenceRationale: The ZIP reference gives the visual benchmark: compact square control, clear selected accent, indeterminate support, and spring-like feedback. Design System keeps ownership of color, type, density, state, icon, motion, and accessibility rules.

anatomy.rule: Names the choice in plain language and remains visible in every state.
Owns size, radius, border, fill, and focus treatment.
Shows check or mixed state only when selected or indeterminate.
Adds optional description, validation, or policy reason without replacing the label.

variants.description: Choice with support text for policy or consequence.
Aggregate choice that can become indeterminate.
Dense row for tables, filters, and settings lists.

checkbox.statePrecedence: disabled > error > focus > indeterminate > checked > unchecked

Energy.decision: Use Energy for box fill, border, status, and disabled contrast.
Energy.behavior: Energy makes selected, mixed, error, and disabled states visible.
Energy.example: Fuel card permission rows show selected accent and clear disabled contrast.
Energy.test: Verify contrast for unchecked, checked, mixed, error, and disabled.
Energy.rejectIf: Color is raw or selection depends on color alone.

Voice.decision: Use Voice for label and support text.
Voice.behavior: Voice keeps the choice readable at each density.
Voice.example: Driver alert choices explain the operational result.
Voice.test: Verify label and support text wrap without clipping.
Voice.rejectIf: The label is hidden or replaced by an icon.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for box size, radius, row spacing, and layout fit.
Frame.behavior: Frame keeps the control fixed while text uses remaining space.
Frame.example: Permission rows stack on phone and align in desktop tables.
Frame.test: Verify no overflow in narrow and wide containers.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only for surrounding surfaces, not for checkbox state.
Depth.behavior: Depth does not replace focus or selection.
Depth.example: A permission panel can have surface depth while the checkbox stays flat.
Depth.test: Verify selection is clear without shadow.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum for hover, focus, and indicator transitions.
Momentum.behavior: Motion confirms state change without delaying the toggle.
Momentum.example: The check indicator appears quickly after selection.
Momentum.test: Verify reduced-motion and quick state feedback.
Momentum.rejectIf: Motion hides value or blocks interaction.

State.decision: Use State for disabled, error, focus, indeterminate, checked, and unchecked precedence.
State.behavior: State precedence decides visuals and interaction.
State.example: Disabled beats checked; error beats focus.
State.test: Verify precedence across all documented states.
State.rejectIf: State is visual only or contradictory.

Tone.decision: Use Tone for direct, outcome-based labels.
Tone.behavior: Tone explains what checking does.
Tone.example: Use 'Enable fuel card' instead of vague consent text.
Tone.test: Verify labels describe outcomes and support text explains risk.
Tone.rejectIf: Copy is ambiguous or legal meaning is guessed.

Growth.decision: Use Growth for reusable selection behavior across settings, filters, and tables.
Growth.behavior: Growth keeps API and states portable as groups scale.
Growth.example: The same contract supports single permission rows and select-all rows.
Growth.test: Verify single and aggregate selection share one state model.
Growth.rejectIf: A product forks checkbox behavior for one screen.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol for check and remove meaning only.
Symbol.behavior: Symbols communicate selected and mixed states.
Symbol.example: Remove symbol means partial selection, not delete.
Symbol.test: Verify symbols match checked and mixed semantics.
Symbol.rejectIf: A decorative icon is placed inside the box.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography for indicator size, weight, fill, and color inheritance.
Iconography.behavior: Icons inherit component state and remain legible.
Iconography.example: Check and remove icons use the same size across densities.
Iconography.test: Verify icon size and fill are tokenized.
Iconography.rejectIf: Icons bypass tokens or change meaning.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility for labels, keyboard, mixed state, focus, errors, and disabled behavior.
Accessibility.behavior: Accessibility makes the boolean value machine-readable.
Accessibility.example: Select-all rows expose mixed state when some children are selected.
Accessibility.test: Verify label, Space toggle, aria-checked mixed, focus, and error association.
Accessibility.rejectIf: The component cannot be operated or understood without sight.

switch.name: Switch
switch.purpose: Use Switch for an immediate on/off setting where the changed state persists and the label explains the active outcome.
switch.referenceRationale: The ZIP reference defines the visual benchmark: 48 by 28 track, expanding thumb on press, clear on/off color, and spring feedback. Design System owns color, type, density, state, motion, and accessibility semantics.

anatomy.rule: Names the setting as the active outcome.
Shows off, on, focus, error, and disabled status without changing size.
Moves and stretches during press to communicate direct manipulation.
Explains consequence or policy only when the label is not enough.

variants.description: High-impact setting that needs human review before use.

switch.statePrecedence: disabled > error > pressed > focus > on > off

Energy.decision: Use Energy for on/off track, disabled, and error color.
Energy.behavior: Energy makes state visible before reading the label.
Energy.example: Driver alerts use accent when on and neutral when off.
Energy.test: Verify contrast for on, off, error, and disabled.
Energy.rejectIf: State depends only on thumb position or raw color.

Voice.decision: Use Voice for labels and support text.
Voice.behavior: Voice explains the setting outcome.
Voice.example: Use 'Send driver alerts' instead of vague on/off copy.
Voice.rejectIf: The label is hidden or ambiguous.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for track, thumb, radius, row spacing, and density.
Frame.behavior: Frame keeps the control stable across states.
Frame.example: Settings rows align in mobile and desktop lists.
Frame.test: Verify no track or thumb clipping across densities.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only for thumb separation.
Depth.behavior: Depth separates thumb from track without decorative elevation.
Depth.example: Thumb shadow stays subtle on both on and off states.
Depth.test: Verify shadow does not replace state.
Depth.rejectIf: Depth is used as the only state signal.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum touch for thumb movement and press stretch.
Momentum.behavior: Momentum communicates direct manipulation.
Momentum.example: Thumb moves with spring and stretches while pressed.
Momentum.test: Verify touch motion and reduced-motion behavior.
Momentum.rejectIf: Motion uses raw duration or curve.

State.decision: Use State for disabled, error, pressed, focus, on, and off precedence.
State.example: Disabled blocks toggling even when on.
State.rejectIf: State is visual only or contradictory.

Tone.decision: Use Tone for direct operational labels.
Tone.behavior: Tone avoids vague settings language.
Tone.rejectIf: Copy hides risk or policy meaning.

Growth.decision: Use Growth for reusable persistent settings across products.
Growth.behavior: Growth keeps API stable across settings surfaces.
Growth.example: The same switch works in driver app and fleet console.
Growth.test: Verify the contract supports settings lists and cards.
Growth.rejectIf: A product forks one-off switch behavior.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol only when an adjacent icon clarifies the setting.
Symbol.behavior: Symbol does not replace label or state.
Symbol.example: A notification icon can support alert settings.
Symbol.test: Verify icons have text labels nearby.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography for optional leading affordances outside the track.
Iconography.behavior: Iconography supports context without entering the track.
Iconography.example: Bell icon appears before alert setting label.
Iconography.test: Verify no decorative icon replaces state.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility for role switch, visible label, keyboard toggle, focus, and state announcement.
Accessibility.behavior: Accessibility exposes on/off state to assistive tech.
Accessibility.example: Switch announces checked state and toggles with Space.
Accessibility.test: Verify role, label, aria-checked, focus, disabled, and error association.
Accessibility.rejectIf: It is implemented as visual-only checkbox without switch semantics.

radio-button.name: Radio Button
radio-button.purpose: Use Radio Button for one option inside a mutually exclusive choice set. The individual control owns selected, unselected, focus, error, and disabled states; grouping rules belong to patterns.
radio-button.referenceRationale: The ZIP reference gives the visual benchmark: 22px circular control, 11px selected dot, 1.5px border, spring dot entry, hover scale, and focus ring. Design System keeps ownership of color, type, density, state, motion, and accessibility rules.

anatomy.rule: Names the single option and remains visible in every state.
Owns fixed size, round shape, border, fill, and focus treatment.
Appears only when the option is selected.
Adds optional description, validation, or policy reason without replacing the label.

variants.description: Option with support text for consequence or scope.
Dense option row for compact decision lists.
High-impact option that needs explicit support copy.

Energy.decision: Use Energy for control border, selected dot, disabled, and error color.
Energy.behavior: Energy makes selected and unavailable options visible.
Energy.example: Route preference options show the selected accent dot.
Energy.test: Verify contrast for selected, unselected, error, and disabled.
Energy.rejectIf: Selection depends on color alone or raw values.

Voice.decision: Use Voice for labels and support text.
Voice.behavior: Voice keeps each option readable and comparable.
Voice.example: Use 'Fastest route' with support text instead of vague mode labels.
Voice.test: Verify label and support text wrap without clipping.
Voice.rejectIf: The option is icon-only or ambiguous.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for circle size, row spacing, radius, and density.
Frame.behavior: Frame keeps the circle fixed while text uses remaining space.
Frame.example: Plan choices align across phone and desktop containers.
Frame.test: Verify the circle does not resize across states.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only on surrounding surfaces, not as radio state.
Depth.behavior: Depth does not replace selected or focus state.
Depth.example: A settings panel can have surface depth while the radio stays flat.
Depth.test: Verify selection is clear without shadow.
Depth.rejectIf: Shadow is used as the selected state.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum for hover scale and selected dot entry.
Momentum.behavior: Motion confirms selection quickly without delaying the choice.
Momentum.example: The selected dot scales in with spring feedback.
Momentum.rejectIf: Motion hides state or uses raw curves.

State.decision: Use State for disabled, error, focus, selected, and unselected precedence.
State.example: Disabled beats selected; error beats focus.
State.rejectIf: State is visual only or contradictory.

Tone.decision: Use Tone for direct option labels.
Tone.behavior: Tone makes each exclusive option easy to compare.
Tone.example: Use 'Manual review' instead of vague risk language.
Tone.test: Verify copy describes the choice outcome.
Tone.rejectIf: Copy hides risk or policy meaning.

Growth.decision: Use Growth for reusable single-choice behavior across products.
Growth.behavior: Growth keeps the atomic option portable while groups evolve into patterns.
Growth.example: The same control works in onboarding, settings, and configuration.
Growth.test: Verify the control is usable without group-specific logic.
Growth.rejectIf: A product forks one-off radio behavior.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol only for adjacent contextual icons, not inside the radio circle.
Symbol.behavior: Symbol supports context without replacing label or dot.
Symbol.example: A route icon may sit next to a preference label.
Symbol.test: Verify icons do not replace selection.
Symbol.rejectIf: Decorative icons enter the control circle.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography only outside the control when context needs it.
Iconography.behavior: Iconography remains supportive and optional.
Iconography.example: Plan icons may support labels in product cards.
Iconography.test: Verify label remains sufficient without icon.

Accessibility.example: Radio announces checked state and changes with keyboard inside a group.

text-area.name: Text Area
text-area.purpose: Use Text Area for longer free-form operational text that needs a visible label, helper or recovery copy, optional character count, and multiline editing.
text-area.referenceRationale: The ZIP reference gives the visual benchmark: full-width multiline surface, 12 by 16 padding, vertical resize, optional bottom-right counter, and fast focus/error transitions. Design System owns tokens, density, state, and accessibility semantics.

anatomy.rule: Names the long-form value and remains visible.
Owns rows, resize, value, placeholder, focus, disabled, and error styles.
Explains purpose, format, privacy, or recovery.
Shows progress toward maxLength without replacing validation.

text-area.statePrecedence: disabled > loading > error > focus > filled > default

Voice.decision: Use Voice for label, placeholder, value, helper, counter, and recovery.

Voice.example: Notes explain visibility to the driver.
Voice.test: Verify label, helper, counter, and error text render.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for full width, rows, padding, resize, and container fit.

Frame.example: Support notes stack on mobile and fit desktop forms.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only on surrounding surfaces.

Energy.decision: Use Energy to define hierarchy, action color, semantic risk, disabled identity, loading identity, borders, and surface contrast. Primary uses sys.energy.action.primary, secondary uses white background with neutral 900 text/border, and outlined uses white background with neutral 200 outline.
Energy.behavior: Primary is action-primary blue filled. Secondary and outlined both keep a white background; secondary uses neutral 900 border/text, outlined uses neutral 200 border with primary text.
Energy.example: Block card uses danger intent; export movements uses secondary or outlined; start route uses primary.
Energy.test: Verify primary uses action-primary blue while secondary and outlined keep white backgrounds and distinct neutral outlines.
Energy.rejectIf: Primary does not use action-primary, secondary/outlined use filled blue, secondary and outlined backgrounds differ, or outlined border is not neutral 200.

Voice.decision: Use Voice to make labels short, verb-first, readable, and role-consistent across densities.
Voice.behavior: Button labels use Ubuntu body/control typography; long labels wrap safely without breaking the control.
Voice.example: Use “Block card”, “Save driver”, “Start route”, not “OK” or “Continue” when consequence is unclear.
Voice.test: Verify label legibility, wrapping, and font mapping across sizes and responsive contexts.
Voice.rejectIf: Generic copy, missing consequence, Edenred display font used for body/control text, or clipped label.

Frame.decision: Use Frame to control button dimensions, padding, gap, radius, touch target, action rows, and responsive composition.
Frame.behavior: Buttons align to containers, support natural or full width, and keep stable layout in rows, sheets, toolbars, and matrices.
Frame.example: Mobile confirmation stacks full-width actions; fleet toolbar keeps natural grouped actions.
Frame.test: Verify no overlap, no horizontal overflow, stable button dimensions, and minimum touch target.
Frame.rejectIf: Hardcoded layout spacing, cramped action rows, horizontal scroll caused by controls, or unstable dimensions.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only to clarify interaction and stacking, not to decorate the component.
Depth.behavior: Hover and pressed states use restrained elevation/inset feedback; overlays and toolbars can override z-index through a component token.
Depth.example: Toolbar ghost actions stay flat; primary dashboard actions can show hover elevation; pressed state uses inset feedback.
Depth.test: Verify rest, hover, pressed, toolbar, and overlay stacking behavior.
Depth.rejectIf: Arbitrary shadows, z-index literals, or elevation that changes hierarchy without interaction.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum to communicate feedback timing, pressed movement, loading activity, and reduced-motion equivalents.
Momentum.behavior: Transitions are explicit properties; pressed movement is tokenized; loading animation stops under reduced motion while state remains clear.
Momentum.example: Save driver shows loading; Start route uses responsive feedback; reduced motion removes spin and movement.
Momentum.test: Verify hover, pressed, loading, and prefers-reduced-motion behavior.
Momentum.rejectIf: transition: all, hardcoded ms/bezier, motion-only meaning, or no reduced-motion path.

State.decision: Use State to resolve the component before visual styling and assistive semantics.
State.behavior: State precedence is disabled > loading > pressed > focus > hover > default.
State.example: Block card goes loading while service responds; permission-blocked action is disabled with reason nearby.
State.test: Verify every documented state and state precedence across variants and intents.
State.rejectIf: State exists only as visual mock, loading equals disabled, or disabled lacks reason.

Tone.decision: Use Tone to match action language and risk language to the product consequence.
Tone.behavior: Default uses neutral direct action; warning uses caution without panic; danger uses repair/consequence language.
Tone.example: Danger action says “Block card” with consequence copy; warning action says “Reset limits” with risk explanation.
Tone.test: Verify labels and adjacent copy follow tone rules for default, warning, danger, and recovery.
Tone.rejectIf: Jokes, vague labels, blame language, or destructive actions without clear consequence.

Growth.decision: Use Growth as adoption and telemetry metadata, not visible decoration.
Growth.behavior: Button emits/declares analytics event and maturity stage while visual UI remains governed by hierarchy, risk, and state.
Growth.example: button.block-card tracks operational action; button.export-movements tracks dashboard utility usage.
Growth.test: Verify event naming exists for product-changing actions and growth metadata does not alter appearance.
Growth.rejectIf: Growth stage appears as decorative UI, missing analytics for critical action, or event name is generic.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol to render Material Symbols by semantic name with accessible fallback policy.
Symbol.behavior: Leading icons use Material Symbols and inherit semantic color from variant/intent; label remains the accessible name.
Symbol.example: block for Block card, route for Start route, download for Export report.
Symbol.test: Verify icon name renders, icon is aria-hidden, and label remains available.
Symbol.rejectIf: Emoji, text glyph, arbitrary SVG, icon-only Button, or missing accessible label.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography to map icon role, density-owned scale, color, and accessible labeling to the button contract.
Iconography.behavior: Icon scale follows Density; icons inherit the label color so danger/warning contrast cannot diverge from text.
Iconography.example: density.sm uses compact icon rhythm; density.md uses normal control icon rhythm; density.lg dashboard and distance contexts use larger icon scale.
Iconography.test: Verify icon scale per Density context and no icon-only Button usage.
Iconography.rejectIf: Icon size hardcoded, icon replaces text, icon role conflicts with action, or icon color does not match label color.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility to guarantee name, role, state, keyboard, focus, contrast, touch target, forced colors, and reduced motion.
Accessibility.behavior: Native button defaults to type button; focus ring is visible; aria-busy marks loading; disabled blocks activation; forced-colors and reduced-motion have fallbacks.
Accessibility.example: Keyboard user can activate Save driver with Enter/Space and see focus before loading starts.
Accessibility.test: Verify role/name, keyboard activation, focus-visible, forced-colors, reduced motion, touch target, loading, and disabled behavior.
Accessibility.rejectIf: No visible label, no focus state, inaccessible loading, color-only meaning, or pointer-only behavior.

Core: Driver or manager completes a primary task safely.
Selection: User chooses one or many valid operational values.
Inputs: User enters operational data with validation and recovery.
Mobile: Driver acts inside constrained touch-first screens.
Maps: Driver finds stations, compares details, and starts route handoff.
Navigation: User moves through hierarchy, steps, pages, and sections.
Dashboards: Fleet manager scans, filters, drills in, and exports evidence.
Configuration: Admin changes users, roles, vehicles, or permissions with audit.
Feedback: System reports status, recovery, progress, or absence.
Overlay: User gets contextual choices without losing origin or focus.
Layout: Content is grouped, revealed, or resized with Frame rules.
Display: Product data is scanned, compared, labeled, or grouped.
Data: User sorts, compares, toggles, and explains data.
Motion: State change communicates cause without becoming decorative.

fallbackProfile: User completes a real product job.

Compact view cannot hide required labels or recovery actions.
Overflow moves into Menu, Bottom Sheet, Dialog, or Pagination depending on group.
Touch, keyboard, and screen reader behavior must remain equivalent.
apiRows: Required for input, selection, data, and navigation components.
State changes copy, ARIA, and visual treatment.
Maps to Frame spacing and Voice scale.
Emits semantic payload, not DOM implementation detail.

testRows: {{title}} renders the correct role, accessible name, visible label, and required state attributes.

{{title}} covers {{states}} with visible, assistive, and recoverable behavior.

warnings.message: Danger needs consequence copy and recovery path near the button.
Warning is for risky but non-destructive actions.

miel.copy: MIEL turns Button into a delegable action decision: the agent can assemble hierarchy, state, and affordance, while the human owns consequence, risk, and recovery.
canDecide: Choose Button when the user is triggering one immediate action.
Select variant, intent, icon, loading, disabled, and full-width behavior from the existing contract.
Write verb-first labels when the action outcome is already clear.
mustAsk: The consequence, recovery path, analytics event, or permission rule is unknown.
The action is destructive, financial, irreversible, or changes access.
The request needs a new system, confirmation pattern, service behavior, variant, or token.
rejectIf: The label is vague, noun-only, or hides the result.
Disabled or loading state appears without reason or recovery.
Danger or warning is used as decoration instead of semantic risk.
The agent invents a new variant, token, or motion rule.
miel.handoff: I am using Button because this is one immediate action. I need confirmation on consequence, recovery copy, and whether the action requires audit or permission handling.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Select as a closed-choice contract: the agent can configure options, value, and state, while the human owns source quality, permissions, and fallback behavior.

rejectIf: Options are not stable enough to expose as label-value pairs.
The component is being used as a search box or free-form input.
Loading, disabled, or error is only visual and lacks helper copy.
The agent creates multi-select behavior before a pattern exists.

states.copy: Combobox states communicate typed filtering, open options, selected value, empty results, error, and disabled behavior.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant stays stable; state controls open, empty, error, selected, and disabled behavior.

full-width.copy: Combobox may fill form columns, filters, and drawers while the option layer follows the field width.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use roomy density for touch contexts and keep typed value, clear action, and option layer legible before placing Combobox inside a larger filter pattern.

viewport-organization.copy: Combobox remains one editable selection field. Viewport rules decide density and option layer width; query orchestration belongs to patterns.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use large density and avoid dense multi-column option content.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep helper copy close to the field and listbox.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density in filter rows only when typed value remains readable.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify label, value, placeholder, options, empty copy, density, and state.

api-foundations.copy: Combobox API exposes one editable selection field. Design System owns field shell, option layer, state, accessibility, density, and motion; product code owns option data and search policy beyond local filtering.

props.notes: Selected value or current input value.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for one known value when typing helps narrow options.
Keep option labels stable and human-readable.
Show empty results copy instead of a blank layer.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use for global search or command palettes.
Do not use for multiple selection.
Do not hide async data loading or permission policy inside the component.

groups.title: Review
items: Confirm local vs remote filtering.
Check keyboard navigation and focus return.
Escalate to a pattern when filtering affects query state, saved views, or multiple fields.

rejectIf: Combobox owns global search or command execution.
Options are visual-only.
Empty results are silent.
It allows multiple selected values.
Raw color, spacing, motion, or typography values are used.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Combobox as one editable selection field: agents can use it when the choices are known and local filtering is enough, while humans confirm data source, empty state, and escalation to patterns.
canDecide: Use Combobox for one known entity list with typed narrowing.
Use Select instead when typing is unnecessary.
Keep option metadata short and text-backed.
mustAsk: Options load remotely, affect URL/query state, or trigger side effects.
The user can select multiple values.
The search behaves like global navigation, commands, or support lookup across systems.
rejectIf: Combobox becomes a command palette, global search, or multi-select.
The option layer lacks visible empty-state copy.
Selected value and active option are not machine-readable.
miel.handoff: I am using Combobox for one editable known-value selection. Please confirm option source, filtering policy, empty copy, keyboard behavior, and whether this should escalate to a pattern.

operational-example.copy: Use Country Selector when a user must choose one country or calling-code context before another component uses that value.

scenario.title: Country and calling code
scenario.meta: SelectCountry reference translated through Flow
rationale: It owns country, flag, calling code, listbox, selected state, and keyboard selection.
Phone Input consumes it instead of duplicating country selector behavior.
The flag supports recognition; country label and calling code remain the source of meaning.

items.rule: Shows selected flag, calling code, and chevron.
Provides decorative recognition only; text remains required.
Lists country label and calling code with selected state.
Allows composition inside Phone Input without changing ownership.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, error, open, focus, default
items: Expose combobox/listbox semantics with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Keep country label and calling code available as text.
Do not use the flag as the only accessible signal.
Escape closes the country list without changing the selected country.
Return focus to the trigger after selection.

variants.copy: Country Selector has a default standalone treatment and an inline treatment for composition inside another field.

states.copy: Country Selector states cover default, open, focus, error, and disabled selection behavior.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines whether the selector is standalone or inline; state still resolves through the same trigger and option layer.

full-width.copy: Country Selector normally keeps intrinsic width; parent fields may stretch it only as part of a larger form composition.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use comfortable density on touch surfaces and keep the option layer wide enough for country names and calling codes.

viewport-organization.copy: Country selection stays a local selector. Phone verification, onboarding, and payment flows decide where it appears.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use inline when paired with a telephone field.

items.title: Tablet

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density inside configuration or support forms.

items: Use for country/calling-code selection.
Compose it inside Phone Input.
Keep labels and codes visible.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not hide country name behind only a flag.
Do not duplicate country selector logic inside phone fields.
Do not use for generic region filters.

groups.title: Review
items: Check country list ownership.
Verify keyboard selection.
Confirm inline usage does not obscure the phone value.

rejectIf: Flag is the only country signal.
Phone Input duplicates selector logic.
Calling code is not text.
Keyboard cannot select an option.

canDecide: Use Country Selector for country and calling-code selection.
Use inline mode inside Phone Input.
Keep country label and calling code visible.
mustAsk: The country source must include compliance or market restrictions.
The selector needs search beyond the default country list.

operational-example.copy: Show what the card helps someone scan or decide: object, value, state, and next available action.

rationale: Each surface frames one object or decision for quick scanning.
Title, value, detail, icon, and state stay visible together.
The parent layout decides grid behavior; Card owns the surface contract.

items.rule: Owns border, radius, shadow, padding, and surface role.
Optional semantic Material Symbol supports recognition without replacing text.
Short object or decision label remains available to assistive tech.
Optional prominent datum or status wraps safely.
Explains scan value, state, or next action.
Hover, focus, selected, loading, error, disabled, and muted resolve before styling.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, loading, error, selected, focus, hover, muted, interactive, default
items: Surface has a clear name from title and supporting text.
Interactive cards expose keyboard focus and activation.
Selected, loading, error, and disabled states are not color-only.
Nested actions keep their own accessible names and focus order.
Long localized content wraps without hiding recovery text.

states.copy: Card state changes surface, text, icon, and recovery path together. Disabled and error states cannot rely on muted styling alone.

variants.copy: Card variants map the ZIP reference to Flow without turning every reference wrapper into a base variant. Default, elevated, minimal, and ghost are surface variants; interactive is behavior, compact/media are compositions, and stats maps to KPI Tile.

reference-compositions.copy: Each item below is rendered from a Flow package component. The reference name shows what appears in the ZIP; the Flow decision explains whether it is a base variant, behavior, composition, or delegated component.

items.label: Interactive
items.flowDecision: Use Card with interactive behavior and state, not a separate variant value.

items.label: Compact
items.flowDecision: Use density and parent layout first; promote only if compact card rows need a reusable contract.

items.label: Media

demo.detail: Beneficios, seguros y combustible con la tarjeta Flow.

items.flowDecision: Use Card composition media while Flow defines image ratio, crop, loading, alt, and media accessibility rules.

demo.title: Sin comisiones
demo.detail: Las recargas entre cuentas Flow no tienen costo.

demo.title: Card · Ghost sobre fondo oscuro (overlays y mapas).

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant controls surface treatment. State controls behavior, feedback, and accessibility without becoming a new surface variant.

full-width.copy: Full-width Card is for mobile stacks, detail sheets, and constrained containers. Desktop dashboards should use grid width from the parent layout.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Mobile cards prioritize one scan value and next action. Desktop cards can support comparison and scan grids.

viewport-organization.copy: Reorganize card content by context. Do not shrink a dashboard card and call it mobile.

items.title: Smartphones + phablets
items.rule: Stack cards and prioritize one scan value plus one next action.

items.title: Tablets + laptops
items.rule: Use two-column comparison when card content remains readable.

items.title: Desktops + TV
items.rule: Use scan grids with larger targets and explicit state labels.

playground.copy: Inspect how role, state, title, value, and description resolve into the Card contract.

api-foundations.copy: Card owns the surface contract. Slots may contain components; product sequencing belongs to patterns.

groups.title: Do
items: Use Card for one scannable object or decision surface.
Keep title, value, description, and state legible.
Let parent layout define grid and width.

groups.title: Do not
items: Nest decorative cards inside cards.
Move product flows into the base component.
Use raw shadows, radii, color, or spacing.

groups.title: Notes
items: Card-led processs such as KPI Card or Mobile Card Overview remain patterns.

mustTest: Renders semantic surface with title, description, optional icon, and state.
Interactive Card is keyboard reachable and preserves focus visibility.
Default, hover, focus, selected, loading, error, disabled, and muted states remain distinct.
Mobile stack, desktop grid, and dense dashboard layouts do not overflow.
Surface, border, radius, padding, elevation, motion, icon, and text resolve through Design System tokens.
rejectIf: Card is used as a decorative wrapper.
Nested decorative cards are required.
Product sequencing is hidden inside the base component.
State is color-only or recovery text is missing.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Card as a scannable surface contract: the agent can configure content, state, and role, while the human decides hierarchy, action meaning, and when the surface becomes a pattern.
canDecide: Use Card when information needs a bounded surface for scanning, comparison, or selection.
Choose default, interactive, selected, muted, loading, error, or disabled state from the documented role.
Arrange title, value, detail, and icon without adding nested cards or local visual rules.
mustAsk: The whole surface triggers navigation, opens a process, or changes data.
The card includes forms, menus, charts, grouped actions, or repeated decisions.
The content hierarchy, risk, or empty/error recovery cannot be inferred.
rejectIf: Card is used as a decorative wrapper for unrelated UI.
Cards are nested to create layout instead of using Frame and layout rules.
A process is hidden inside the base component instead of moving to a pattern.
State relies only on color or has no recovery path.
miel.handoff: I am using Card because the user needs to scan an object, value, and state. I need confirmation on whether the surface is purely informational or should escalate to a pattern.

operational-example.copy: Use Input when someone must enter or edit a short free-form value with visible guidance, validation, and recovery.

rationale: Accepts values that cannot be pre-enumerated.
Keeps label and helper visible while typing.
Makes validation and recovery explicit.

items.rule: Groups label, input, helper, and state so the field moves as one component.
Names the value and remains visible before, during, and after input.
Holds value, placeholder, focus, disabled, loading, and error styles.
Explains format, source, validation, or recovery.
Optional leading icon or non-interactive qualifier supports the value without replacing copy.
Optional reveal or clear action uses the internal Field Action primitive: icon-only, no default container, field-owned density, visible focus, and accessible state.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, loading, error, focus, filled, default
items: Visible label is required; placeholder cannot be the only name.
Helper and error text are associated with the input.
Error uses aria-invalid and gives a fix, not only a color.
Disabled and loading states are announced and block misleading edits.
Keyboard focus remains visible and follows document order.

states.copy: States communicate editability, progress, validation, and value condition. The field keeps its label and helper visible in every state.

variants.copy: Variants describe the capture role. State still owns default, filled, loading, error, focus, and disabled behavior.

demos.label: Password
demos.helper: Use reveal only to verify entry

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant gives the field role; state controls behavior. State precedence wins when role and condition compete.

full-width.copy: Full-width Input is for mobile forms, sheets, and constrained containers. Desktop layouts should inherit width from their grid or form group.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Mobile fields stack with full labels and helper text. Wider layouts can group fields, but should not hide recovery or force crowded columns.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport behavior follows Density and Frame: one column when space is tight, grouped rows only when labels, helper text, and states remain readable.

items.title: Smartphones + phablets
items.rule: Stack fields full-width with visible helper or recovery copy.

items.title: Tablets + laptops
items.rule: Group related fields when labels and helper text remain readable.

items.title: Desktops + TV
items.rule: Use larger inspector fields for remote viewing or review surfaces.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify capture role, label, value, helper text, state, density, mono values, and qualifiers before moving the field into a form or filter.
playground.snippet: <Input label="Driver ID" value="MX-2048" helperText="Active driver record" />

api-foundations.copy: The API keeps free-form input controlled, visible, and recoverable. Density owns scale; state owns behavior.

props.name: placeholder
props.notes: Hint only; never the only label.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Blocks edits; explain with helper text.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Capture role. It sets native type/input mode defaults without changing state rules.

props.name: prefix
props.notes: Optional short qualifier before the value; avoid using it as the only currency identifier.

props.name: mono
props.notes: Uses code typography for plates, IDs, card fragments, or amounts.

props.name: suffix
props.notes: Adds a short non-interactive qualifier such as MXN, USD, EUR, kg, t, plate, or card.

props.name: type
props.notes: Native input type override when variant defaults are not enough.

props.name: align
props.notes: Value alignment, usually end for numeric capture.

props.name: revealable
props.notes: Adds the show/hide affordance for password-like values.

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Called with normalized value and display metadata for numeric, currency, and unit variants.

groups.title: Do
items: Keep the label visible.
Use helper text for expected format.
Preserve value during validation.
Use Field Action only for actions that operate on the current field value.

groups.title: Do not
items: Do not use placeholder as the only label.
Do not clear input on error.
Do not hide disabled or loading reason.
Do not place an autonomous Icon Button inside the field surface.

groups.title: Escalate
items: Use Select for bounded options.
Use a pattern for suggestions, masks, or multi-field flows.
Ask before adding product-specific parsing or a new Field Action behavior.

mustTest: Label, value, placeholder, helper, suffix, mono value, and error render from props.
Focus, typing, Tab, disabled, loading, and error states work.
Helper and error text are associated with the input.
Field Action reveal toggles value visibility, aria-pressed, and aria-label without adding a visible button container.
Responsive examples do not overflow at small viewports.
rejectIf: Placeholder is the only label.
Error is only a color.
Value disappears during loading or validation.
Scale bypasses Density or uses raw spacing.
A field-local action is implemented as a one-off icon button style instead of the Field Action primitive.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Input as a short free-form value contract: the agent can place and configure the field, while the human owns meaning, validation policy, and operational risk.
canDecide: Use Input when the value cannot be selected from a finite list.
Configure label, placeholder, helper, value, density, icon, suffix, and visible state.
Place the field in a form, filter, stack, or row when grouping is already clear.
mustAsk: Validation, mask, formatter, required rule, or error copy is unknown.
The value affects money, permissions, identity, compliance, or audit.
The experience needs suggestions, autocomplete, scanner input, or a multi-field pattern.
rejectIf: Placeholder is the only label.
Error, disabled, or loading state removes the value or explanation.
The field is used for closed-choice data that should be Select.
The agent invents a formatter, mask, or validation rule.
miel.handoff: I am using Input because the value is short and free-form. I need confirmation on validation, risk level, and the recovery copy for invalid input.

operational-example.copy: Use Checkbox when someone needs to turn one independent choice on or off, or show that a group is partially selected.

items.label: Enable fuel card
items.description: Allow purchases for assigned stations.

items.label: Send driver alerts
items.description: Notify the driver before balance changes.

items.label: Select all visible drivers
items.description: 3 of 12 drivers selected.

rationale: Each row is an independent boolean choice.
Indeterminate communicates partial selection without pretending the value is final.
Labels and support text keep operational consequences visible.

items.rule: Write the choice as the outcome of checking the box.
Keep the square stable across checked, unchecked, focus, error, and disabled states.
Use check for selected and remove for mixed; never use decorative icons inside the box.
Explain consequence, policy, or recovery only when the label is not enough.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, error, focus, indeterminate, checked, unchecked
items: Associate every checkbox with a visible label.
Support keyboard focus and Space toggling.
Expose indeterminate as mixed, not checked.
Keep focus visible around the control box.
Associate error text with the checkbox when validation is present.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate checked, mixed, or error states.

states.copy: States must make the value, mixed condition, focus, validation, and disabled behavior visible without changing the label.

variants.copy: Variants describe the row structure around the same boolean control. They do not change selection semantics.

demos.label: Descriptive
demos.description: Show balance alerts before a charge is approved.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant and state combine without changing precedence: disabled wins first, then error, focus, mixed, checked, and unchecked.

full-width.copy: Checkbox rows may fill the available width, but the control box keeps its fixed size and the label owns the remaining space.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Responsive layout changes the row stack, not the boolean meaning or state priority.

viewport-organization.copy: Organize Checkbox rows by available reading space: stack on narrow screens, align with tables on wide screens, and avoid dense clusters on touch surfaces.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use full-width rows with large density.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Stack short groups before moving into two-column layouts.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Align with table rows or permission columns, keeping labels readable.

playground.copy: Use the playground to confirm label length, support text, density, checked value, and mixed state before using Checkbox in a system.

api-foundations.copy: Checkbox API exposes value, mixed state, support text, validation, and disabled behavior while Design System foundations own styling.

props.name: required
props.notes: Marks a required consent or setting.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for independent boolean choices.
Use indeterminate only for partial aggregate selection.
Keep the label as the checked outcome.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use for mutually exclusive choices.
Do not hide the label behind an icon.
Do not make error color the only signal.

groups.title: Review
items: Confirm legal or consent copy with the human owner.
Check keyboard and mixed-state behavior.
Test label wrapping at narrow widths.

rejectIf: The checkbox has no visible label.
Mixed state is only visual.
The box changes size across states.
The row becomes a radio group replacement.
Disabled copy removes the reason for lockout.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Checkbox as an explicit boolean or partial-selection contract: the agent can configure value and state, while the human owns meaning, consent, policy, and consequence.
canDecide: Use Checkbox for one independent yes/no choice or a select-all aggregate.
Set checked, unchecked, indeterminate, focus, error, and disabled when product logic is explicit.
Place rows in settings, filters, tables, or permission groups when grouping already exists.
mustAsk: The choice affects consent, money, permissions, identity, compliance, or legal wording.
The difference between unchecked and indeterminate is not defined.
The row belongs to a mutually exclusive set that may require Radio instead.
rejectIf: The checkbox has no visible label.
Mixed state is decorative or not backed by child selections.
The control replaces Radio for mutually exclusive choices.
Disabled state hides why the choice cannot change.
miel.handoff: I am using Checkbox because this is an independent boolean choice or partial group selection. I need confirmation on the checked outcome, policy wording, and indeterminate logic.

operational-example.copy: Use Switch when a setting turns on or off immediately and the new state persists.

items.label: Send driver alerts
items.description: Notify before balance changes.

items.label: Auto-approve fuel stops
items.description: Requires manager review before use.

items.label: Offline spending mode
items.description: Unavailable for this fleet policy.

rationale: The setting has a persistent on/off value.
The label describes what becomes active.
The thumb motion confirms direct manipulation.

items.rule: Names the active outcome of the setting.
Shows on/off, focus, error, and disabled state without changing size.
Moves with spring and stretches on press to show direct manipulation.
Explains consequence, policy, or recovery only when needed.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, error, pressed, focus, on, off
items: Use role switch and expose checked state.
Associate every switch with a visible label.
Support keyboard focus and Space toggling.
Keep focus visible around the track.
Do not rely on color alone for on/off state.
Associate error or policy text when present.

states.copy: States communicate value, focus, press, validation, and disabled behavior while preserving the label.

variants.copy: Variants describe the settings row around the same on/off control. They do not change switch semantics.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant and state combine without changing precedence: disabled wins first, then error, pressed, focus, on, and off.

full-width.copy: Switch rows may fill the available width, but the track keeps its fixed size and the label owns the remaining space.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Responsive layout changes the settings row, not the on/off meaning or state priority.

viewport-organization.copy: Organize Switch rows by setting context: stack on narrow screens, align with configuration rows on wide screens, and keep track size stable.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use full-width rows with large density.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Group related settings before moving into columns.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Align with inspector rows and keep labels readable.

playground.copy: Use the playground to confirm label, support text, density, on/off value, and state before placing Switch in a settings system.

api-foundations.copy: Switch API exposes persistent on/off value, support text, validation, and disabled behavior while Design System foundations own styling.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for persistent on/off settings.
Keep the active outcome in the label.
Use immediate feedback when value changes.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use for multi-select choices.
Do not hide policy meaning in helper text only.
Do not use when a Save step owns the final value.

groups.title: Review
items: Confirm high-impact settings with the human owner.
Test keyboard and screen reader state.
Check label wrapping at narrow widths.

rejectIf: The switch has no visible label.
The value does not persist.
It replaces Checkbox in multi-select lists.
The track or thumb changes size unpredictably.
Motion bypasses Momentum tokens.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Switch as a persistent on/off setting contract: the agent can configure state and placement, while the human owns meaning, policy, risk, and whether the effect is immediate.
canDecide: Use Switch when a setting persists immediately after it changes.
Set off, on, focus, pressed, error, and disabled when product logic is explicit.
Place rows in settings, configuration, or inspector surfaces when the setting group already exists.
mustAsk: The setting affects money, permissions, compliance, automatic approvals, or notifications.
The effect is delayed, requires Save, or does not persist.
The label needs legal, policy, risk, or operational wording.
rejectIf: Switch is used for a one-time action instead of a persistent setting.
The value does not persist or needs a separate submit action.
The control replaces Checkbox for multi-select or consent.
Disabled or error state lacks explanation.
miel.handoff: I am using Switch because this is a persistent setting with an immediate on/off value. I need confirmation on what on means, when it takes effect, and whether risk requires review.

operational-example.copy: Use Radio Button when one option belongs to an exclusive decision and the option itself needs a visible label, state, and optional support text.

items.label: Fastest route
items.description: Prioritize arrival time for active deliveries.

items.label: Lowest fuel cost
items.description: Use lower-cost stations even if route time increases.

items.label: Manual review
items.description: Requires dispatcher approval before route starts.

rationale: Each row is one option in a mutually exclusive decision.
The selected dot makes the current choice visible without hiding the label.
Group orchestration belongs to a future Radio Group pattern, not the atomic control.

items.rule: Names the option in plain language and remains visible in every state.
Keeps a fixed circular shape across selected, unselected, focus, error, and disabled states.
Scales in only when the option is selected.
Explains consequence, scope, or recovery only when the label is not enough.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, error, focus, selected, unselected
items: Use a native radio input or equivalent platform role.
Keep a visible label associated with the control.
Expose checked state to assistive technology.
Do not hide group question, validation, or keyboard orchestration inside the atomic control.
Disabled options remain readable and do not change value.

states.copy: States communicate whether the option is available, selected, focused, invalid, or unavailable without changing the circle size.

variants.copy: Variants describe how much context one radio option carries. They never replace the parent question or group behavior.

demos.label: Descriptive
demos.description: Balance arrival time and fuel cost.

demos.label: Critical
demos.description: Requires dispatcher approval before route starts.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant and state behavior stays atomic: selected state changes the dot, error changes border and support text, and disabled blocks interaction.
