Energy.subtitle: Color, semantic roles and product intensity

Iconography.subtitle: Functional glyphs, grid rules and accessible icon usage

primaryParagraphs: When color appears in Design System, it always carries meaning. This discipline allows users to interpret the interface quickly and confidently.
Energy translates Design System's design principles into visual meaning through color.
Color in Design System is never decorative — it communicates intent, hierarchy, and feedback.
Energy ensures users can immediately recognize: primary actions, system feedback, critical states, and surface hierarchy.
By doing so, Energy makes Design System predictable and visually learnable.
Voice defines the complete typographic and communication system: families, weights, scale, line heights, numerals, labels, guidance, repair copy, and confirmations.
Display, heading, and numeral roles use Edenred Black. Body, subtitles, captions, UI labels, tables, and code use Ubuntu.
Voice gives teams a stable hierarchy so product copy can be scanned before it is read.

secondarySections.title: Architecture
secondarySections.description: The Voice layer follows the same ref -> sys -> comp chain as the reference system.
secondarySections.code:
FONT FAMILIES
brand -> Edenred Black, Ubuntu fallback: Display + Heading + Numeral
sans  -> Ubuntu, system fallback: Label + Paragraph
mono  -> Ubuntu Mono fallback: Code + Token names

COMPOSITE ROLES
Display xl/l/m/s
Heading xl/l/m/s
Numeral xl/l/m/s
Label xl/l/m/s
Paragraph xl/l/m/s
Caption
Overline
Code

RULE
No raw font-family, font-size, line-height, or weight in components.

primaryParagraphs: Frame governs all spatial relationships: spacing, sizing, grid, breakpoints, density modes, and page rhythm.
Every gap, padding, margin, panel, and grouping decision derives from a shared scale.
Density is declared at the layout or page level. Components inherit density; they do not invent one-off spacing.

secondarySections.title: Spacing Scale Design
secondarySections.description: The scale is tuned for practical use, not strict mathematics.
secondarySections.code:
BASE UNIT
4px

SPACE SCALE
0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128

GRID
mobile  -> 1 column, 16px margin
tablet  -> 6 columns, 24px gutter
desktop -> 12 columns, 24px gutter, 48px margin

DENSITY
compact      -> tighter gaps, smaller type step
default      -> standard operating rhythm
comfortable  -> larger touch and reading rhythm

primaryParagraphs: Depth defines the spatial metaphor of the interface: how surfaces stack, how elevation communicates hierarchy, and how overlays create focus.
Depth governs shadows, z-index, surface tinting, backdrop treatment, and temporary layers.
The model keeps maps, sheets, drawers, menus, dashboard cards, and critical messages from competing for the same plane.

secondarySections.title: Elevation Model
secondarySections.description: Design System uses numeric levels with semantic aliases for product surfaces.
secondarySections.code:
ELEVATION SCALE
Level 0 -> Canvas: no shadow
Level 1 -> Raised: cards, list items
Level 2 -> Floating: menus, popovers
Level 3 -> Overlay: sheets, dialogs, focused panels
Level 4 -> Critical: toast, high-priority interruption

SHADOW COLOR
Light: branded navy shadow
Dark: black shadow with boosted opacity

Z-INDEX RANGES
0      base content
100    dropdowns and popovers
200    sticky headers and toolbars
1000   overlays and modal backdrops
1100   toasts and critical notices

primaryParagraphs: Momentum governs all animation and transition in the system. It ensures motion is intentional, consistent, and respectful of user preferences.
Every moving element uses Momentum tokens. Components do not use raw durations or easing values.
Motion explains cause, continuity, status, and transition. It never exists only to make the interface feel lively.

secondarySections.title: Motion Categories
secondarySections.description: These categories mirror the reference Momentum documentation.
secondarySections.code:
MICRO-INTERACTIONS
0-100ms: hover, press, focus, toggle feedback

TRANSITIONS
150-350ms: tabs, sheets, dropdowns, route panel changes

CHOREOGRAPHY
300-500ms: dashboard loading, staggered cards, onboarding sequences

CONTINUOUS
cycle duration: spinners, progress, shimmer, sync

REDUCED MOTION
replace translation and scale with opacity, focus placement, and instant state changes

primaryParagraphs: State defines the formal interaction model for all Design System artifacts: which states exist, how they appear, and how conflicts resolve.
State delegates color to Energy and depth to Depth. Its job is the structural pattern: overlay, ring, border, opacity, message, announcement, or suppression.
State also defines what assistive technologies should receive when a component changes condition.

secondarySections.title: State Composition
secondarySections.description: States can coexist. Precedence prevents incoherent UI.
secondarySections.code:
COMPOSITION
selected + hover   -> selected base + hover overlay
selected + focus   -> selected base + focus ring
error + focus      -> error border + focus ring
loading + hover    -> loading wins; hover suppressed
disabled + error   -> disabled wins; error visual suppressed

REQUIRED STATES
default, hover, pressed, focus, selected, loading, disabled, error, success

primaryParagraphs: Tone defines the structural framework for how the product communicates through text.
It governs error messages, empty states, confirmations, labels, warnings, and instructional copy.
Tone does not write every sentence. It defines the pattern that makes content actionable, respectful, progressive, and consistent.

secondarySections.title: Communication Principles
secondarySections.description: The reference model treats communication as structure, not flavor.
secondarySections.code:
PRINCIPLES
1. Actionable over informational
2. Blame the system, not the user
3. Progressive disclosure
4. Consistent tense
5. No jargon

CONFIRMATIONS
past tense: Changes saved, Route started

ACTIONS
present imperative: Save changes, Start route

WARNINGS
conditional future: This will block card use

primaryParagraphs: Growth defines product learning signals and the maturity model for system evolution.
It helps teams understand adoption, migration, deprecation, and whether a pattern is ready to become a shared contract.
Growth events must be structured, non-PII, and attached to product context.

secondarySections.title: Event Schema
secondarySections.description: Events are named and structured so teams can learn without scattering tracking code.
secondarySections.code:
EVENT SHAPE
event: system.component.interaction
component: Button
variant: primary
context: routes.stationDetail
action: click
properties: semantic, non-PII details

EVENT TYPES
impression
interaction
completion
abandonment
error

Symbol.primaryDescription: Symbol is not about producing illustrations. It is about designing a visual architecture.
primaryParagraphs: Symbol defines a modular visual system capable of generating characters, scenarios, environments, motion-ready assets, and narrative micro-scenes governed by Design System tokens.
The system is modular: body, posture, accessory, environment, object, and scale compose scenes from finite parts.
The system is token-driven: palette, stroke, proportions, spacing, and theme variants derive from the same foundations as product UI.

cards.label: Reduction
cards.title: Earn complexity
cards.copy: Default to fewer elements. Let a dominant shape carry the message.

cards.label: Narrative
cards.title: Minimum story
cards.copy: A small visual mismatch or object can create curiosity without noise.

cards.label: Environment
cards.title: Scene as character
cards.copy: Spatial relationships explain what is happening before detail does.

cards.label: Motion-ready
cards.title: Implied timing
cards.copy: Static compositions should suggest the moment before or after action.

secondarySections.title: Modular Architecture
secondarySections.description: Compose infinite scenes from finite primitives.
secondarySections.code:
CHARACTER PRIMITIVES
Body, posture, accessory, scale

ENVIRONMENT PRIMITIVES
Ground plane, architecture, context objects, atmosphere

COMPOSITION RULES
Background layer -> light planes and atmosphere
Mid-ground layer -> architecture and context objects
Foreground layer -> character and accessory
Ground plane -> baseline and optional steps

RULE
Environment provides context without competing for attention.

primaryParagraphs: Iconography defines the icon system: grid, stroke, optical adjustments, semantic categories, naming, color, and the consumption API.
Icons are functional glyphs, not artwork. They aid recognition, navigation, action identification, and state comprehension.
Design System uses Material Symbols as raw material, but Design System owns the semantic mapping and accessibility policy.

secondarySections.title: Icon Grid & Rules
secondarySections.description: The reference model treats icons as constrained functional glyphs.
secondarySections.code:
GRID
Base: 24 x 24px
Live area: 20 x 20px
Stroke: 1.5px
Corner radius: 1px terminals, 2px enclosed shapes

SIZING
xs 12px
sm 16px
md 20px
lg 24px
xl 32px

SEMANTIC CATEGORIES
Navigation, Action, Status, Object, Toggle, Finance, Currency, Chart

EVERY ICON MUST
have one meaning
have category assignment
have accessible labeling rules

primaryParagraphs: Accessibility preserves access through keyboard, touch, screen reader, contrast, motion, language, and recovery.
It is product-specific in Design System because drivers and fleet managers often work under constrained, mobile, operational, or high-risk conditions.
Accessibility is not a final checklist; it is a foundation that changes component, pattern, and template behavior.

secondarySections.title: Access Contract
secondarySections.description: Every artifact must keep a usable path when a modality or permission is unavailable.
secondarySections.code:
REQUIRED PATHS
keyboard path
touch path
screen reader name and state
contrast-safe role
reduced-motion equivalent
permission denied recovery
offline or stale-data recovery

RULE
If one modality fails, the task must still have a documented route.

fallback.ledeTemplate: {{title}} defines a system-level rule that must be visible in design, code, content, accessibility, and agent output.
columns: {{title}} clarifies what the system should emphasize or prevent.
The rule is semantic before it is visual.
The same foundation must work in mobile driver flows and desktop fleet operations.
Agents should be able to read the rule and produce consistent UI decisions.

Energy.lede: When visual intensity appears in Design System, it always carries meaning. Energy lets drivers and fleet managers understand what is actionable, successful, risky, broken, or simply structural.
columns: Energy translates product priority into color, emphasis, rhythm, and status.
Energy is never decoration. It communicates intent, hierarchy, and feedback.
Energy keeps dashboards calm while making operational exceptions unmistakable.
Energy makes the product learnable because the same signal means the same thing everywhere.

Voice.lede: Voice defines how Design System writes, labels, explains, repairs, confirms, and escalates. It combines Edenred Black display/title/numeral typography with Ubuntu body/UI text.
columns: Labels name the object precisely before describing the action.
Guidance appears before risk, not after the user fails.
Repair copy explains what happened and what can be done next.
Confirmation copy records consequence, owner, and next state.

Frame.lede: Frame governs all spatial relationships: page rhythm, panels, density, grid, responsive behavior, and what belongs together.
columns: Every gap, padding, and grouping decision comes from a shared spatial scale.
Frame separates primary work from supporting context.
Density is declared at the surface level and inherited by components.
Frame prevents ad-hoc layout fixes from becoming design language.

Depth.lede: Depth defines the spatial metaphor of the interface: how surfaces stack, how overlays focus attention, and how elevation communicates hierarchy.
columns: Depth separates canvas, raised content, floating controls, overlays, and critical feedback.
Elevation uses tokenized shadows and z-index ranges instead of arbitrary stacking.
Maps, sheets, menus, and dashboards use the same spatial grammar.
Depth tells users what is persistent, temporary, contextual, or blocking.

Momentum.lede: Momentum governs animation and transition so movement explains cause, continuity, status, and system activity without becoming decoration.
columns: Durations map to micro-interactions, transitions, choreography, and continuous feedback.
Easing distinguishes elements entering, exiting, moving continuously, or changing state.
Stagger organizes dense content like dashboards and route alternatives.
Reduced motion preserves meaning when translation, scale, or continuous animation is minimized.

State.lede: State defines which interaction states exist, how they combine, and which state wins when several conditions happen at once.
columns: Hover, focus, pressed, selected, loading, disabled, error, and success are formal states.
Disabled and loading suppress conflicting affordances before components render.
Focus and error can coexist because one explains navigation and the other explains validation.
State maps visual behavior to assistive technology semantics.

Iconography.lede: Iconography defines functional glyph rules: grid, size, category, naming, color, and accessible labeling.
columns: Icons are functional glyphs, not decorative art.
Material Symbols are consumed through semantic categories and tokenized size/color roles.
Icon-only actions require accessible names and predictable hit targets.
Missing icons should fail visibly during documentation and implementation.

energyPalette.title: Energy Palette
energyPalette.description: Energy uses a strict 10-step scale per family. No helper colors, no one-off tints, and no extra brand accents live inside the foundation palette.

energyFilledStatus.title: Filled Status Contrast
energyFilledStatus.description: Filled status surfaces choose the color ramp and foreground together. Do not cross from dark foreground to light foreground inside one interaction sequence.

rows.title: Warning

rows.title: Action
rows.use: Action-colored filled controls when neutral primary is not the right semantic.

voiceTypography.title: Typography System
voiceTypography.description: Voice uses the same structure as the reference zip: a 4 x 4 semantic grid plus utility roles. Edenred is reserved for display and headings; Ubuntu carries product text, UI labels, captions, and code.

groups.name: Paragraph
variants: Your card is safe. No charge was made.
Enable location to find nearby stations faster.
Fuel limits update after the next sync.

utilities: Dense token references and small annotations.

voiceTokens.title: Voice Tokens
voiceTokens.description: The foundation now exposes the same base ingredients as the zip: families, weights, size scale, letter spacing, and line height. Components should consume semantic sys.voice roles, not raw CSS values.

frameSpacing.title: Spacing Scale Design
frameSpacing.description: Frame uses a 4px base with deliberate jumps for page rhythm. The important part is the use case attached to each step, not the number by itself.

frameGrid.title: Responsive Grid
frameGrid.description: The zip does not document grid as an abstract token table. It shows how the product grid changes by tier and where margins/gutters come from.

frameDensity.title: Density Remapping
frameDensity.description: Density is declared at the page or surface level. Controls, cards, gaps, and grid specifications respond together through sys.frame tokens.
frameDensity.demoCopy: Padding, gap, radius, and control height shift as one system.

frameTokens.title: Frame Tokens
frameTokens.description: Frame follows the zip as a spatial foundation: spacing, radius, control heights, content widths, borders, documentation measures, breakpoints, and responsive grid.

frameSystem.title: Responsive And Density
frameSystem.description: Frame resolves layout decisions before components render. Pages declare density and viewport tier; components inherit spacing, control heights, radii, and grid behavior.

explorers.description: A focused product demo replaces abstract cards. It shows how the foundation changes real driver or fleet-manager UI.

action: Primary route action is available and should be visually discoverable without overwhelming the map.
success: The driver completed the route handoff and the system can confirm without adding noise.
warning: Fuel price or station availability may affect the decision, but the user can still continue.
error: The route cannot start because location permission is blocked or data failed.
surface: The panel recedes so content can be scanned while keeping hierarchy clear.

columns: Mobile card
Tablet inspector
Desktop dashboard

label: Card status
Available balance and usage limit
Label copy
Use labels to name the object before explaining state.
guidance: Enable location to find nearby stations faster.
Guidance appears before failure and explains why the permission matters.
repair: Try another payment method or contact fleet support.
Your card is safe. The transaction was not completed and no charge was made.
confirm: Fuel purchases are now blocked for this card.
Confirmations use past tense and record the result of the action.

Depth.title: Station detail
Depth.copy: Depth communicates whether this surface is base content, raised context, floating menu, overlay, or critical feedback.

duration: Touch feedback uses the 160ms spring rhythm; base and slow durations handle reveal and larger transitions.
easing: Touch uses spring, enter uses ease-out, exit uses the lifecycle close curve, move uses in-out, and linear is reserved for continuous loading.
stagger: Items appear in a controlled cascade instead of arriving all at once. Dense lists use faster stagger than featured content.
tokens: Documented sys tokens are what components consume; ref tokens remain the raw scale behind the system.
reduced: Meaning survives without large movement by using focus placement, opacity, and instant state changes.

Momentum.reducedCopy: Large translations become opacity, focus placement, and instant state changes while the same information remains available.

neutral: Your card can be used at enabled stations and merchants.
assistive: Enable location to sort nearby stations by distance and route time.
urgent: Fuel purchases are paused until the fleet manager reviews this card.
repair: Check your connection or search by city while location recovers.

seed: Document the use case, owner, tokens, and first validation path before broad adoption.
stable: The artifact has token coverage, tests, examples, and adoption guidance.
measured: Usage, task success, and support signals are reviewed before expansion.
deprecated: Migration path, replacement, and removal window are visible to all teams.

keyboard: Every route action, sheet, and map fallback can be reached without pointer input.
contrast: Text, icons, map pins, and status colors keep usable contrast in light and quiet modes.
motion: Route, sheet, and confirmation transitions have non-positional alternatives.
recovery: Denied permissions, offline data, and failed map loading always provide another path.

Preference management.copy: Delegates settings groups, form sections, validation, save/reset, and danger confirmation to Preference Management.

Settings Workspace.standard: This template is the full product settings workspace and composes governed preference patterns instead of owning controls directly.
Settings Workspace.screenSystem: The screen system separates settings section navigation from preference content while keeping state, density, and danger confirmation in the Flow cascade.
Settings Workspace.informationArchitecture: Navigation follows settings work: profile, notifications, theme mode, security details, and danger-zone actions.
Settings Workspace.primary: User updates workspace preferences, saves changes, and confirms risky settings actions without leaving the governed Flow surface.
qualityGates: Section selection keeps Tabs, root state, and preference content synchronized.
Settings controls are delegated to Preference Management and Settings, not locally rendered by the template.
Danger-zone behavior is delegated to Confirmation Dialog through Preference Management.

patternDetails.Preference Management: Owns settings groups, Form Section blocks, Settings controls, Confirmation Dialog, save/reset, validation, permission, and danger-zone state.

hero.title: A design system that can ship a fleet product.
hero.lede: Design System now works as a documentation product: foundations, primitives, components, patterns, templates, stack decisions, and agent-readable specifications connected through real product flows.

coverage.title: Coverage is broad. Depth is uneven.
coverage.copy: This is the current working map: some layers are structurally updated, while components, patterns, and templates still need richer product examples and interactions.

items.label: Components
items.reference: Button gold, Select interactive, group standard for the rest

items.label: Patterns
items.reference: Pattern playbook applied, examples still need richer flows

items.label: Templates
items.reference: Domain templates exist, screen systems need sharper differentiation

documentationStatus.title: Batch the work, then promote the winners to gold.
documentationStatus.copy: We should not move one page at a time forever. The fast path is fixing shared templates first, then promoting high-impact artifacts into hand-authored examples.

items.detail: Role groups, architecture, visual explanation, contract, spec, agent prompt.
Overview, live-style demo, responsibilities, token chain, API, spec, agent prompt.
Button is gold. Select now has interactive examples. Remaining components inherit family standards and need richer live demos by group.
Decision trees, failure modes, journeys, metrics, research, contracts. Needs more product-specific screens per pattern family.
They exist as domain templates, but need stronger screen systems, dashboard layouts, mobile route/card flows, and configuration flows.

visualMigration.title: Use the ZIP as a benchmark, not a new source of truth.
visualMigration.copy: The next phase is to match the ZIP's product polish through Design System's existing foundations, primitives, contracts, and audit gates.

items.label: Migration rule
items.detail: Design System foundations and primitives stay in charge: Energy, Voice, Frame, Depth, Momentum, State, Density, Charts, Maps, and Accessibility.

items.label: Migration rule
items.detail: Use the ZIP as a benchmark for polish, mobility examples, product screens, state richness, and interaction rhythm.

items.label: Migration rule
items.detail: Do not import raw color, typography, public size props, inline styles, hand-written charts, or direct map assumptions.

items.label: Start small
items.detail: Button and Select prove the benchmark quality first, then Card, Icon Button, Badge, Chip, Field, and Input.

architecture.title: Nothing skips a layer.
architecture.copy: Every route, dashboard, card action, and permission system traces through the same inheritance model.
